about_lead: “Volunteers” is a youth volunteering association born from the dream of a group of young people from Catania: to be the overwhelming proof that, in the 21st century, being human is not just a possibility, but an ancestral duty that has never faded.
about_body: Volunteers is, without euphemism, an act of rebellion: we rebel against apathy, unbridled individualism and the passivity of modern society. Rooted in altruism and empathy, Volunteers is a light of hope both for those who help and for those who are helped.

about_story_description: We know we are not alone: we know we are not the only ones who feel the need to be human. That is why our very first goal is to make the opportunity to do good accessible to everyone.

project_citizens_description: We bring to life active citizenship projects started by students and young professionals. From caring for our cities to supporting those who have been left behind: we act here and now to build genuine relationships and a shared future.
project_citizens_approach: The project starts by identifying places worth reviving, continues with workshops to share recycling and maintenance techniques, and ends with community events that strengthen the bonds between residents. The goal is a neighbourhood that is better cared for, livelier and more involved, through concrete actions that last over time.

project_children_description: Every week our volunteers spend afternoons with children and teenagers in the most fragile neighbourhoods: helping with homework, playing in the courtyard and simply being there. Being a friendly older face for a child can change the way they see school, their city and their future.
project_children_approach: Alongside school support we run neighbourhood play centres, creative workshops in middle schools and games in paediatric wards, and in summer we organise camps full of sport and friendship. We work with families, schools and local associations so that every activity becomes a lasting point of reference, not a one-off event.

project_medical_intro: A project that brings warmth and presence where illness makes days longer.
project_medical_description: A hospital stay is not only a medical matter: it is waiting, fear and loneliness. Our volunteers visit paediatric wards and care facilities with games, clown therapy and time to listen, so that patients and their families feel they are not facing it alone.
project_medical_approach: Outside the hospital we promote blood donation among young people together with local donor associations, and we organise health awareness days in schools and universities. Every volunteer is trained before entering a ward, because care starts with knowing how to be present with respect.

project_international_approach: When an emergency strikes, our network of groups mobilises to collect essential goods and support the partners working on the ground. Throughout the year we build partnerships between students of different countries, with exchanges and shared projects that turn cultural differences into friendship.

news_article_project: This story is part of the project
news_youth_record_p1: This year more than 10,000 young people and university students signed up to volunteer with us, the highest number since Volunteers was born in Catania. Behind that number there are faces, friendships and afternoons spent where they are needed most.
news_youth_record_p2: Many of them had never volunteered before. They found us through a friend, a talk at their university or a post on social media, and chose to give a few hours a week to a food drive, a homework club or a hospital ward.
news_youth_record_heading: Why young people are choosing solidarity
news_youth_record_p3: When we ask new volunteers why they joined, the answers are surprisingly similar: they want to do something concrete, they want to meet people who share their values and they want to have fun while doing it. Solidarity, for them, is not a sacrifice but a way of living their city.
news_youth_record_quote: I came for one afternoon and stayed for the people. Now it is the best part of my week.
news_avis_bologna_excerpt: Our volunteers joined the Avis Bologna Provincial Assembly to talk about young people, blood donation and how to make giving a habit.
news_avis_bologna_p1: This September a group of Volunteers from Bologna took part in the Provincial Assembly of Avis, the association that brings together blood donors across the province. It was a chance to listen, share our experience and meet the people who keep donation going every day.
news_avis_bologna_p2: We were invited to tell how we reach students and young workers: short talks in universities, donation days organised together with friends and a lot of word of mouth. Many of our volunteers donated for the first time thanks to someone who went with them.
news_avis_bologna_heading: Making donation part of student life
news_avis_bologna_p3: Together with Avis we discussed how to bring more young people to donation centres, from flexible time slots to information in several languages for international students. We left with new ideas and the promise of a joint donation day this autumn.
news_avis_bologna_quote: Donating blood is the simplest way to say that someone else's life matters to you.
news_intergenerational_workshops_excerpt: Grandparents and grandchildren around the same table: our recycling workshops turned waste into games, crafts and new friendships.
news_intergenerational_workshops_p1: For three Saturdays in a row, the community centre in our neighbourhood filled up with children and older residents. The goal was simple: learn to recycle better, together. The result was much more than that.
news_intergenerational_workshops_p2: Older participants taught the children how things used to be repaired and reused, while the children explained the new sorting rules and turned bottles and cardboard into toys. Our volunteers kept the materials coming and the conversations going.
news_intergenerational_workshops_p3: At the end of the workshops, families took home a small guide to separate collection written by the children themselves. Several older residents asked us to continue with gardening and cooking sessions, and we are already planning the next round.
news_intergenerational_workshops_quote: I taught them how to fix a chair; they taught me where the yoghurt pots go. Fair exchange.
news_neighbourhood_festival_excerpt: Music, food and games in the square: 300 neighbours spent an afternoon together at the party organised by our volunteers.
news_neighbourhood_festival_p1: It started as an idea during a clean-up of the local park: why not bring people back to this square for something other than passing through? Two months later, 300 residents of all ages filled it for an afternoon of music, food and games.
news_neighbourhood_festival_p2: Local shops donated snacks and drinks, a school band played, and children took over the space with chalk and relay races. Our volunteers ran the stands, welcomed newcomers and made sure the older residents had a seat in the shade.
news_neighbourhood_festival_heading: A square that belongs to everyone again
news_neighbourhood_festival_p3: The best moment came at sunset, when neighbours who had lived on the same street for years introduced themselves for the first time. We collected dozens of ideas for the square's future, and many people signed up to help with the next event.
news_neighbourhood_festival_quote: I have lived here for twenty years and today I finally know my neighbours' names.
news_catania_urban_excerpt: In the heart of Catania, residents and volunteers are redesigning a forgotten corner of the city together, one workshop at a time.
news_catania_urban_p1: Catania is where Volunteers was born, and it is where we keep testing new ways of caring for the city. This spring we started a participatory renewal project in a historic neighbourhood where an abandoned courtyard had become a dumping ground.
news_catania_urban_p2: Instead of arriving with a finished plan, we asked residents what they wanted. Over four evening meetings, families, shopkeepers and students drew, argued and voted. The answer was clear: shade, benches, a space for children and plants that survive the Sicilian summer.
news_catania_urban_p3: With the plan in hand, volunteers and residents cleared the rubbish, painted the walls and built planters from recycled pallets. The work is not finished, but the courtyard is already alive again, and the residents have formed a group to look after it.
news_catania_urban_quote: We did not come to fix the neighbourhood; we came to build it with the people who live here.
news_rotterdam_excerpt: A new delegation in the Netherlands: a group of students in Rotterdam has brought the Volunteers spirit to one of Europe's busiest ports.
news_rotterdam_p1: It all started with a few Italian students on exchange in Rotterdam who missed their Saturday afternoons with Volunteers. They talked to their classmates, found a couple of local organisations willing to host them and, a few months later, the first Dutch group was born.
news_rotterdam_p2: Today the Rotterdam delegation brings together students from more than ten countries. They help at a neighbourhood food bank, organise language cafés for newcomers and spend time with older residents who live alone.
news_rotterdam_p3: Starting a group abroad means learning a new city, new rules and a new language. The Rotterdam volunteers did it with the support of the international office and the experience of the Italian groups, and they are now ready to welcome anyone who wants to join.
news_rotterdam_quote: We speak different languages, but on Saturday afternoons we all speak Volunteers.
news_rotterdam_quote_cite: A member of the Rotterdam delegation
news_clown_therapy_excerpt: Red noses, bubbles and a lot of listening: how our volunteers bring play into the paediatric wards of Rome's hospitals.
news_clown_therapy_p1: Every week a group of volunteers in Rome puts on a red nose and walks into a paediatric ward. They do not perform a show; they knock on doors, ask permission and adapt to whoever is on the other side, whether it is a child who wants to laugh or a parent who needs a moment of rest.
news_clown_therapy_p2: Before their first shift, each volunteer follows a training course on hygiene, privacy and the basics of clown therapy. The most important lesson is to read the room: sometimes the best game is a whisper, a puppet or simply sitting in silence.
news_clown_therapy_heading: Play as a form of care
news_clown_therapy_p3: Doctors and nurses tell us that a visit can change the mood of an entire day, making treatments easier to face. For our volunteers, it is a lesson in presence and humility that they bring back to every other part of their lives.
news_clown_therapy_quote: A child told me I was the only one in the hospital who never wore a white coat. I took it as a compliment.
news_empathy_forum_excerpt: Talks, workshops and a full theatre: a recap of our annual forum on empathy, where hundreds of young people asked what it means to be human today.
news_empathy_forum_p1: Every year we invite volunteers, students and friends to stop for a day and think about why we do what we do. This year's forum on empathy filled a theatre with young people from all our Italian and European groups.
news_empathy_forum_p2: The morning opened with talks from educators, doctors and volunteers who shared stories from the field. In the afternoon, participants split into workshops on active listening, loneliness among young people and how technology can bring us closer instead of apart.
news_empathy_forum_p3: The word that came up most often was the one that defines us: rebellion. Against apathy, against individualism, against the idea that caring for others is naive. We left the theatre with new friendships and a long list of ideas for the year ahead.
news_empathy_forum_quote: Empathy is not a feeling you wait for. It is a choice you make every Saturday afternoon.
news_milan_meals_excerpt: Every evening, more people are knocking on the door: in Milan our volunteers now serve twice as many hot meals as a year ago.
news_milan_meals_p1: When we started distributing hot meals in Milan, a small group of volunteers prepared a few dozen portions a week. Today, thanks to hundreds of new volunteers and the generosity of local shops, the number of meals served has doubled.
news_milan_meals_p2: Behind every meal there is a chain of people: those who collect surplus food, those who cook, those who pack and those who go out in the evening to hand it over. And there are conversations, because a hot meal is often the start of a relationship with someone who has been invisible for too long.
news_milan_meals_p3: The growing numbers also tell a harder story: more families and older people are struggling to make ends meet. That is why, alongside the meals, our volunteers help people find their way to local services, from health clinics to job centres.
news_milan_meals_quote: People remember the soup, but what they thank us for is that we stop and talk.
news_palermo_workshops_excerpt: Murals, theatre and a lot of colour: our creative workshops in Palermo's middle schools are giving students a new way to tell their story.
news_palermo_workshops_p1: This year our Palermo group brought creative workshops into three middle schools in neighbourhoods where school dropout rates are among the highest in the city. Every week, volunteers and students met to paint, write and act.
news_palermo_workshops_p2: The workshops were designed with the teachers to fit into the school timetable. Students chose the themes themselves: their neighbourhood, their dreams, what makes them angry and what makes them proud. The result was a mural, a short play and a lot of new confidence.
news_palermo_workshops_p3: At the end of the year, families and teachers gathered for the unveiling of the mural in the school courtyard. Some of the students who had struggled most to speak in class presented their work in front of everyone. For us, that was the real result.
news_palermo_workshops_quote: At first they said they could not draw. By the end, they were arguing about which shade of blue to use for the sea.
news_trento_perugia_excerpt: Two new local groups join the Volunteers family: students in Trento and Perugia have started their first projects in their cities.
news_trento_perugia_p1: Our map keeps growing. This spring two new groups were born in Trento and Perugia, both started by university students who had met Volunteers in other cities and wanted to bring the same energy home.
news_trento_perugia_p2: In Trento the first volunteers chose to spend time with older people living alone, with weekly visits and afternoons of games. In Perugia they started with a food drive at the university canteen and are now planning a homework club for children in the historic centre.
news_trento_perugia_heading: How a new group is born
news_trento_perugia_p3: Every new group starts with a small team, a first project and a lot of questions. Our national office supports them with training, materials and contacts, and the older groups share what they have learnt. The rest comes from the passion of the people on the ground.
news_trento_perugia_quote: We thought we would be ten. At the first meeting there were forty of us.
news_trento_perugia_quote_cite: A founder of the Perugia group
news_pediatric_games_excerpt: Board games, drawings and a lot of laughter: our volunteers spent an afternoon with the children in Catania's paediatric ward.
news_pediatric_games_p1: For children in hospital, afternoons can feel endless. That is why our Catania group organised an afternoon of games in the paediatric ward, with board games, drawing and stories for every age.
news_pediatric_games_p2: The volunteers moved from room to room with a trolley full of materials, adapting to each child's energy and treatment. Those who could not leave their bed played cards on a tray; those who could joined a drawing competition in the common room.
news_pediatric_games_p3: Parents told us that for a few hours their children forgot where they were. The ward staff have asked us to come back regularly, and we are now organising a monthly schedule with a trained team of volunteers.
news_pediatric_games_quote: She lost at every game and still asked when we would be back. That was the best answer.
news_madrid_excerpt: Volunteers arrives in Spain: in Madrid, our first Spanish group has launched a project with children and families in the city's southern neighbourhoods.
news_madrid_p1: Spain was the first country outside Italy where Volunteers took root, and Madrid is where our first Spanish project has now begun. The group brings together Spanish students and young people from across Europe who live in the city.
news_madrid_p2: Their first project is an after-school club in one of the southern neighbourhoods of Madrid, run together with a local parish and a community association. Twice a week, volunteers help children with homework and then move to the courtyard for football and games.
news_madrid_p3: Starting abroad means adapting our way of working to a new culture, new partners and new needs. The Madrid volunteers have brought their own ideas, from language exchanges for families to weekend trips to the city's parks, and the Italian groups are already learning from them.
news_madrid_quote: The children correct my Spanish and I help them with maths. Everyone learns something.
news_acireale_camp_excerpt: A week of sport, games and friendship: our summer camp in Acireale welcomed children from the neighbourhoods where we work all year round.
news_acireale_camp_p1: For many of the children we meet during the school year, summer means long days at home with little to do. That is why our Acireale group organised a week-long summer camp, open to children from the neighbourhoods where we run our after-school clubs.
news_acireale_camp_p2: Each day started with sport on the beach and continued with workshops, treasure hunts and swimming lessons. Volunteers from several Sicilian groups took turns as coaches, cooks and storytellers, and many of them took time off work to be there.
news_acireale_camp_p3: The camp was not about winning or learning a specific skill. It was about giving children a week to feel free, safe and part of a group. On the last evening, around a bonfire, they asked us to promise that we would do it again next year. We did.
news_acireale_camp_quote: By Wednesday nobody remembered which neighbourhood anyone came from. They were just one team.
news_university_talks_excerpt: From lecture halls to the field: our new talk series brings stories of volunteering into universities across Italy.
news_university_talks_p1: Most of our volunteers are university students, and many of them first heard of us in a classroom. This year we decided to make it official, with a series of talks in universities in Catania, Rome, Milan and Bologna.
news_university_talks_p2: Each talk brings together a volunteer, a professor and someone from a partner organisation. They share stories from the field, answer questions and explain how students can get involved, even with just a few hours a month.
news_university_talks_heading: Volunteering as part of your education
news_university_talks_p3: We believe that volunteering is not a break from studying but part of growing up. It teaches teamwork, responsibility and how to listen, skills that no exam can measure. Several universities are now discussing ways to recognise volunteering in their students' careers.
news_university_talks_quote: I came for the credits and stayed for the people. Now I run the group in my faculty.
news_rome_food_drive_excerpt: Over two tonnes of food in a single weekend: the food drive organised by our Rome group in the city's supermarkets.
news_rome_food_drive_p1: For one weekend, our volunteers in Rome stood at the entrances of dozens of supermarkets across the city with a simple request: add something to your shopping for someone who needs it. By Sunday evening, more than two tonnes of food had been collected.
news_rome_food_drive_p2: Pasta, tinned food, milk, baby food and cleaning products filled hundreds of boxes. Behind the scenes, other volunteers sorted, weighed and loaded everything onto vans heading for the food banks and parishes we work with all year.
news_rome_food_drive_p3: What struck us most was not the quantity but the people. Pensioners who gave a single packet of pasta, families who filled a whole trolley, cashiers who came out to thank us. The food will reach hundreds of families in the coming months.
news_rome_food_drive_quote: An older gentleman gave us one tin of beans and apologised that it was not more. It was worth everything.
